messages:
maria: customer reporting intermittent 429s + long tail latency on bursts. happens after a quiet period (~20m). they say requests succeed if retried a few seconds later.

maria: pasted their quick repro:
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-xxxx' \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-rlhf-smol","input":"short prompt"}'
```
response head excerpt:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rate-limit-type: burst
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 5
content-length: 0
```

maria: they attached a small flamegraph showing one long spike in scheduling + many small waits. customer is on Dedicated but with relatively low committed qps; they rely on burst.

tj: can we confirm this is quota exhaustion (token-bucket) vs perceived throttling from batching?

neil: quick guess: when traffic is idle we drain batch queues quickly -> cold kv-cache. on first burst continuous-batcher groups requests to reach ideal batch size which adds a few hundred ms. multiple retries/clients piling up will look like "throttling" and then token-bucket hits cause 429.

neil: two separate issues: 1) KV prefix cold misses causing slower first-token latencies, 2) tenant burst bucket used up because many retries are stamped as separate requests.

sara: do we have the request ids for a sample window to check routing and bucket counters?

maria: sent logs privately (not in thread). example header from failing request: `x-request-id: rc-8a2f`

support-bot: Noted. Automated check: tenant sk-acme-xxxx has burst_limit=100/sec, committed_qps=10, current_burst_balance=0 at 2026-03-01T14:12:03Z.

tj: ok config matches symptoms. next steps: 1) repro script that avoids aggressive client-side retries, 2) try warming kv-cache before burst, 3) short-term bump of burst allowance if customer needs spike capacity.

maria: customer wants a short repro we can run from our side. neil, can you drop a small script that simulates their burst pattern but paces retries?

neil: dropping script in thread:
```
# stress-burst.sh - send 120 requests over 6s, no immediate retries
for i in $(seq 1 120); do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-xxxx" \
    -d '{"model":"gpt-rlhf-smol","input":"hi"}' &
  sleep 0.05
done
wait
```
This reproduces the 429s locally for me when kv-cache is cold. If I run a warmup pass (10 reqs 30s before) the 429s mostly disappear.

tj: that's a good repro. we should also check batching queue latencies. neil, can you capture the continuous-batching histogram for this tenant during the run?

neil: captured and attached (private). summary: scheduling latency spikes to ~350ms on the first wave, steady-state ~20ms. kv-cache miss rate ~72% for prefix "acme:session:" on first 60s.

sara: recommend mitigation path:
- advise customer to add a short warm-up call pattern before expected bursts (5-10 warmup calls 1 min prior).
- reduce client retry aggressiveness (exponential backoff with jitter).
- enable short-lived prefetch in routing policy for Dedicated tenants (ops change).

maria: ops change needs approval. tj, can infra temporarily raise burst_limit for acme while we do fixes? customer has an upcoming demo.

tj: I can bump burst_limit to 250/sec for 6 hours from console and watch metrics. will also add alert if sustained over 60s. doing it now. :white_check_mark:

support-bot: Action taken: burst_limit for sk-acme-xxxx set to 250/sec until 2026-03-01T20:12:03Z by tj.

maria: customer confirmed lower error rate after bump. still seeing ~20% higher p99 latencies on initial waves. they are ok with warmup suggestion for now.

neil: longer-term we should consider:
- prefetching KV prefixes for Dedicated tenants with predictable keys,
- adaptive batching: reduce batch wait time during first N seconds after idle,
- bucket smoothing to allow microbursts that don't punish cold-cache patterns.

tj: filed infra ticket INF-4521 to investigate prefetch + adaptive batching. I'll link logs and the repro.

maria: thanks all. i'll send the customer the repro script + recommendations and close the ticket once INF-4521 has an owner. :pray:
